## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

Python API or bindings
<!-- Choose one:
- C++ frontend API or graph construction
- Python API or bindings
- FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL
- Build, packaging, or installation
- CI or test infrastructure
- Documentation or samples
- Benchmarks or performance
- Not sure
-->

## Summary

<!-- What changed? Keep the scope concise. -->
Add `graph.serialize(as_bytes=True)` and support `bytes` input in
`graph.deserialize()`. The default `serialize()` return type remains
`list[int]` for backward compatibility.

## Why

<!-- What problem does this solve, and why is this approach appropriate? -->

Graph serialization produces a binary payload. The existing `list[int]`
representation comes from the automatic conversion of C++
`std::vector<uint8_t>`, rather than the semantics of the data.

`bytes` represents this payload more naturally and avoids constructing
a Python list with one entry per byte, reducing conversion overhead and
memory usage. The serialized format and contents remain unchanged.

Unlike graph serialization, device properties and kernel cache
serialization produce JSON text, so their `str` return types remain
appropriate.

## Related issues

<!-- Use "Fixes #123" or "Related to #123" where applicable. -->

## API and compatibility impact

<!-- Note public API, supported GPU/cuDNN/CUDA/Python versions, performance, or backward-compatibility changes. Write "None" if not applicable. -->

This behavior predates the nanobind migration: both pybind11 and nanobind
automatically convert `std::vector<uint8_t>` to `list[int]`.

Since graph serialization produces binary data, `bytes` is a more natural
representation. This PR adds bytes support while preserving the existing
API behavior.

Would it be preferable to return `bytes` by default and accept only `bytes`
for binary deserialization? That would be a breaking API change.

## Testing

<!-- List exact commands and results. If something was not tested, explain why. -->

- Linux regular and stable-ABI builds: each **129 passed, 1 skipped,
  9 deselected**.
- Verified identical payloads and GPU execution after deserialization
  from both lists and bytes.
- Strict `abi3audit`: no ABI violations or version mismatches.
- Pre-commit checks passed.
- Windows runtime was not tested; validation was performed under WSL/Linux.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Graph serialization can now return compact binary `bytes` with the `as_bytes` option; the default list-of-byte-values format remains available.
  * Graph deserialization now accepts binary `bytes` inputs, including bytes subclasses, alongside supported existing formats.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

-        untouched."""

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Binary serialization preserves the legacy format and executable plan."""
+
+import cudnn
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.L0
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def serialized_conv(cudnn_handle):
+    graph = cudnn.pygraph(
+        io_data_type=cudnn.data_type.HALF,
+        intermediate_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT,
+        compute_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT,
+        handle=cudnn_handle,
+    )
+    x = graph.tensor(dim=[2, 8, 16, 16], stride=[2048, 1, 128, 8], data_type=cudnn.data_type.HALF)
+    w = graph.tensor(dim=[16, 8, 3, 3], stride=[72, 1, 24, 8], data_type=cudnn.data_type.HALF)
+    y = graph.conv_fprop(image=x, weight=w, padding=[1, 1], stride=[1, 1], dilation=[1, 1])
+    y.set_output(True)
+    graph.build([cudnn.heur_mode.A, cudnn.heur_mode.FALLBACK])
+    return graph, x, w, y
+
+
+def test_serialize_bytes_preserves_default(serialized_conv):
+    graph, *_ = serialized_conv
+    legacy = graph.serialize()
+    binary = graph.serialize(as_bytes=True)
+    assert type(legacy) is list
+    assert type(binary) is bytes
+    assert graph.serialize(as_bytes=False) == legacy
+    assert binary == bytes(legacy)
+    assert b"\0" in binary  # Embedded NULs must not truncate the blob.
+    native = graph._lowered_graph
+    assert type(native.serialize()) is list
+    assert native.serialize(as_bytes=True) == binary
+    for target in (graph, native):
+        with pytest.raises(TypeError):
+            target.serialize(True)  # The new option is keyword-only.
+
+
+class BytesSubclass(bytes):
+    pass
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("payload_type", [list, tuple, bytes, BytesSubclass])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("handle_form", ["implicit", "positional", "keyword"])
+def test_deserialize_bytes_executes(serialized_conv, cudnn_handle, payload_type, handle_form):
+    graph, x, w, y = serialized_conv
+    payload = payload_type(graph.serialize())
+    restored = cudnn.pygraph(handle=cudnn_handle)
+    if handle_form == "positional":
+        restored.deserialize(cudnn_handle, payload, enforce_precompiled=True)
+    elif handle_form == "keyword":
+        restored.deserialize(handle_=cudnn_handle, pyobj=payload, enforce_precompiled=True)
+    else:
+        restored.deserialize(payload, enforce_precompiled=True)
+    stream = torch.cuda.ExternalStream(cudnn.get_stream(cudnn_handle))
+    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        weight = torch.ones([16, 8, 3, 3], device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16).to(memory_format=torch.channels_last)
+        output = torch.empty([2, 16, 16, 16], device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16).to(memory_format=torch.channels_last)
+        workspace = torch.empty(restored.get_workspace_size(), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8)
+        for value in (1, 2):
+            image = torch.full([2, 8, 16, 16], value, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16).to(memory_format=torch.channels_last)
+            output.fill_(float("nan"))
+            restored.execute({x: image, w: weight, y: output}, workspace, handle=cudnn_handle)
+            expected = torch.nn.functional.conv2d(image, weight, padding=1)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(output, expected, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    stream.synchronize()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("payload", [b"", b"invalid serialized graph"])
+def test_deserialize_malformed_bytes_matches_list(cudnn_handle, payload):
+    errors = []
+    for data in (list(payload), payload):
+        graph = cudnn.pygraph(handle=cudnn_handle)
+        with pytest.raises(Exception) as exc:
+            graph.deserialize(data)
+        errors.append((type(exc.value), str(exc.value)))
+    assert errors[0] == errors[1]

reviews.body:
**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `3529fd524297` against base `a7269d7607db`.

Thank you for your contribution! I found no blocking issue. Keeping list[int] as the default and adding opt-in bytes is the appropriate compatibility choice; changing the default or removing legacy input support would need a separate API migration. The explicit-length copies preserve embedded NULs, and the bytes path provides a measurable conversion and memory benefit without changing the serialized format.

Validation: Built the exact-head Linux Release extension for CPython 3.10 and a separate stable-ABI extension, then loaded and exercised the latter on CPython 3.14. Native H100 with the freshly built extension: all 15 new serialization tests and 4 API-signature compatibility tests passed. Three additional legacy tests passed for JSON rejection under enforce_precompiled, device-properties deserialization and replacing a deserialized plan's binding layout; one separately selected higher-level kernel-cache test was deselected by the L0/L1 filter. Independent regular/stable-ABI probes passed list, tuple, bytes and bytes-subclass round trips, JSON structural deserialization, the device-properties/no-handle path, and malformed/empty/truncated blob error parity. Head and baseline produced the identical 2,940-byte payload and hash. CPU serialization spot check, two head and two baseline rounds with 500 samples per mode: default-list medians stayed about 43.3-43.6 us; opt-in bytes measured 33.5-33.7 us on CPython 3.10. Python container sizes were 23,576 bytes for the list versus 2,973 bytes for bytes. This is one small built convolution graph, with serialization itself included.

Limitations: Windows and ARM64 were not executed locally. Stable-ABI validation here covered building, loading and serialization contracts; the GPU execution pytest suite ran with the regular CPython 3.10 extension. The timing and container-size results describe this payload and host, not all graph sizes. I did not independently repeat the author's abi3audit run.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
